sentences.english_text: The doorman at the theater had a son who was a computer expert working in Washington, D.C.
, the capital of the United States.
The doorman was writing a letter to his son as Drippy came out of the basement and started upstairs.
All the performers were leaving the theater.
Drippy saw Mr. Harris and his rabbits.
I'm not going to let him make me disappear again, Drippy said.
And Drippy climbed up on the table where the doorman was writing his letter.
Drippy stepped on the sheet of paper.
The doorman who had finished the letter folded it up and put it in an envelope and sealed it.
Drippy was trapped inside the envelope.
Hey, let me out of here.
But no one could hear him.
The doorman put a stamp on the letter and threw it into a mailbox where it stayed until the next morning.
That is why neither the wind nor the mouse nor the cricket nor the bluebird could find Drippy.
He had disappeared again.
Early the following morning, the mailman picked up the letter with Drippy inside it, put it in his mail sack and carried it to the post office.
The post office was an enormous building with hundreds of workers.
Drippy's letter was dumped on a huge table with thousands of other letters and mail clerks began sorting them.
Each letter had a zip code and when the post office worker saw a number, he would throw it into a slot where that zip code belonged.
Drippy felt himself being thrown into the air and into a slot.
And a few minutes later, he was picked up again, thrown into a truck and driven to an airport.
Of course, Drippy sealed inside the letter had no idea where he was.
At the airport, a sack with hundreds of letters in it was put aboard a cargo plane.
And a few hours later, Drippy was in Washington, D.C.
It was not until the following morning that the letter with Drippy in it arrived at the desk of the son of the stage doorman.
The son was glad to get the letter from his father.
He opened it quickly.
For the first time in two days, Drippy could breathe fresh air.
He leaped out of the envelope, took a deep breath and looked around.
He was in a very strange room.
There were dozens of enormous machines in the room.
They were computers, but Drippy did not know that.
All around him were men in uniforms.
I wonder where I am, thought Drippy.
